fields.description:
Initiate the automatic configuration for a clocking group.

Typically this function will identify the need for unicast clock leaders
in the clocking group, based on whether devices span multiple subnets / VLANs.

If the need for unicast clock leaders is established, up to 2 suitable devices
will be selected in each subnet / VLAN and the unicast clocking option will be enabled for them.

If no need for unicast clock leaders is established (e.g. when all devices belong to the same subnet / VLAN)
the unicast clocking option will be disabled for all devices in the clocking group.

To manually configure unicast clocking, use the DeviceClockinUnicastSet mutation.
fields.name: ClockingGroupAutomaticallyConfigure

fields.description:
Configure a clocking group including PTP settings, AES67 or SMPTE 2110 modes.
A clocking group is a collection of clocking configuration including PTPv1 and PTPv2 parameters,
typically including a unique system-generated PTPv1 subdomain.
Devices associated with a Clocking Group are intended to clock together.
By default, each domain has a separate clocking group, although multiple domains
can share a clocking group, allowing media to be shared between them.
fields.name: ClockingGroupSet

fields.description:
Enable or disable PTPv1 unicast delay requests for a device
In subnets with many devices, enabling unicast delay requests reduces multicast traffic
and can help to overcome bandwidth limitations
fields.name: DeviceClockingPTPV1UnicastDelayRequestSet

fields.description:
Override certain domain preferences for an individual device, 
including PTPv2 priorities and RTP settings.

Overriding domain-wide PTPv2 priorities with lower values
can force the selection of a device as the PTPv2 clock leader in the domain.
fields.name: DeviceClockingPreferencesOverridesSet

fields.description:
Set or clear the preferred leader option for a device.
When enabled, the preferred leader option influences the Best Clock Master Algorithm (BMCA)
to preferentially choose the device as the PTPv1 clock leader, given all other factors.
fields.name: DeviceClockingPreferredLeaderSet

fields.description:
Set or clear the sync to external option for a device.

  Some devices have their own clock source internally,
  or have the capability to connect directly to an external clock source
  via non-networked means (such as via a coaxial connection).

  For these devices, enabling sync to external will cause the device to use its own
  external clock rather than PTP clock as its synchronisation leader.

  Devices with sync to external enabled will generally become the PTP clock leader for
  other devices in the same clocking group.


Sync to external is only supported in some Dante platforms and devices.
fields.name: DeviceClockingSyncToExternalSet

fields.description:
Set or clear the unicast clocking option on a device.

When enabled, the device will be able to function as a unicast boundary clock if required.

For domains that span 2 or more subnets / VLANs, at least one active unicast boundary clock
is required in each subnet to synchronise clocking across the subnet boundary.

It is recommended to have 2 devices in each subnet enabled for unicast clocking
to provide redundancy if the device acting as the unicast boundary clock fails.

Also see the mutation 'ClockingGroupAutomaticallyConfigure'.
fields.name: DeviceClockingUnicastSet

fields.description:
Set (or clear) the name of a device.

The device name is used to identify the device and also to establish and maintain media routing.

If the name of a transmitting device is changed, active media subscriptions will fail and
should be re-established e.g. using the mutation DeviceRxChannelsSubscriptionSet.

Devices maintain a default name that is set in the factory, and is used as the device name
in the case that no other name has been set (e.g. AVIOAO2-0123ab)

Note, the device name is not a unique identifier in the system; use deviceId instead.
fields.name: DeviceNameSet

fields.description: Set extended 'Dante Device Link' parameters on a device.
fields.name: DeviceParametersSet

fields.description:
Set the policy (access roles) for a device when controlling additional device functions
or other devices in the network.

Examples are where one device has the capability to control media routing on other devices
in the same domain, or non-Dante functions on the device itself.

Note that the availability of these roles for a particular device depends on its in-built capbilities
as well as the default roles set by the original equipment manufacturer on the device.
fields.name: DevicePolicySet

fields.description: Set (or clear) channel subscriptions on an RX device
fields.name: DeviceRxChannelsSubscriptionSet

fields.description:
Unenroll (unassign) device(s) from their domain, with an option to clear device configuration.

After unenrollment, devices will return to their unmanaged state
and can be accessed locally using Dante Controller.
fields.name: DevicesUnenroll

fields.description:
Assign a clocking group to a domain.

Domains have their own unique clocking group at the time the domain is
created.

To allow domains to share clock leaders and media (when available) they
need to share the same clocking group.

This mutation can combine domains into a clocking group by associating
domain A with the clocking group already associated with domain B.

This mutation also allows a domain to leave a shared clocking group by
being assigned a new unique clocking group with a default clocking mode.

This is a no-op if the request is to:
1. Join a clocking group and the domain is already in the clocking group.
2. Leave a clocking group and the domain is already in its own unique
   clocking group.
fields.name: DomainClockingGroupAssign

Remove a domain.
Note, a domain cannot be removed whilst there are devices enrolled in it.

    v2DomainNumber: 127,
    v2Priority1: 128,
    v2Priority2: 128,
    RTP.rxLatency: 2000,
    RTP.prefixV4: 69

Unique identifier (ID) for the clocking group.

To find this identifier for the clocking group associated with a domain,
query Domain.clockingGroupId or Domain.clockingGroup.id
inputFields.name: clockingGroupId
clockingGroupId

inputFields.description:
Set a pre-configured clocking mode.
The clocking mode dictates some PTP defaults and also controls other system features such as RTP flow creation.
DEFAULT: Only use Dante Clocking. Only PTPv1 will be enabled unless overridden by custom PTP settings (Dante Director Professional only).
AES67: In AES67 clocking mode, both PTPv1 and PTPv2 will be enabled, with following PTP default settings if not specified:
    PTPv1: true,
    PTPv2: true,
    dantePriorities: true,
    v2DomainNumber: 0,
    v2Priority1: 248,
    v2Priority2: 248,
    RTP.rxLatency: 2000,
    RTP.prefixV4: 69
SMPTE: In SMPTE 2110 clocking mode, both PTP V1 and V2 will be enabled, with following default settings if not specified:
    PTPv1: true,
    PTPv2: true,
    dantePriorities: false,
    v2DomainNumber: 127,
    v2Priority1: 128,
    v2Priority2: 128,
    RTP.rxLatency: 2000,
    RTP.prefixV4: 69
inputFields.name: mode

inputFields.description: Advanced customizable PTP settings (Dante Director Professional only).
inputFields.name: ptp

inputFields.description: Advanced customizable RTP Flow settings (Dante Director Professional only).
inputFields.name: rtp

inputFields.description:
('Danteness'): If enabled, devices will try to sync to the clocking group first. Enabled by default.
For example: when dante priority enabled, when a device with better internal clock joins the subnet, the device will attempt to sync to the existing leader using its clocking offset and slowly take over as the new leader.
This cannot be disabled in clocking groups set to a 'PTPv1 only' mode.
inputFields.name: dantePriorities

inputFields.description: If enabled, devices will try to be clocking followers only. Disabled by default.
inputFields.name: followerOnly

inputFields.description: If enabled, Dante devices will prefer to use PTPv1 clocking over PTPv2 clocking. Enabled by default.
inputFields.name: v1

inputFields.description:
A unique system-generated PTPv1 subdomain tag for the clocking group (or '_DFLT' when in AES67 mode).
Used to isolate the PTPv1 clocking within a multicast subnet.
Assigned randomly on site creation.
inputFields.name: v1SubdomainName

inputFields.description: If enabled, Dante devices will able to clock with 3rd party PTPv2 devices including PTPv2 capable switches. Disabled by default.
inputFields.name: v2

inputFields.description: Frequency of announce messages sent to follower clocks. Log Mean Interval (LMI) value.
inputFields.name: v2AnnounceInterval

inputFields.description:
Used to isolate the PTPv2 clocking within a multicast subnet.
Devices with the same PTPv2 domain number will attempt to clock together.
inputFields.name: v2DomainNumber

inputFields.description: TTL = time to live, the number of hops allowed before the PTPv2 packet is discarded. Typical value is 16.
inputFields.name: v2MulticastTtl

inputFields.description:
PTPv2 Priority 1 is used in the first pass of the Best Clock Master Algorithm (BMCA) for clock leader election.
Smaller values indicate higher priority.
inputFields.name: v2Priority1

inputFields.description:
PTPv2 Priority 2 is used in the second pass of the Best Clock Master Algorithm (BMCA) for clock leader election.
Smaller values indicate higher priority.
inputFields.name: v2Priority2

inputFields.description: Frequency of sync messages sent to follower clocks. Log Mean Interval (LMI) value.
inputFields.name: v2SyncInterval

inputFields.description:
The second octet of the IPv4 multicast address range for RTP flows, 239.xx
The prefix must match between devices to share RTP flows.

inputFields.description: Latency setting (buffer size) for RTP flows in microseconds e.g. 2000 (2 milliseconds)
inputFields.name: rxLatency

inputFields.description:
Packet time is the length of audio, in microseconds, per RTP packet sent.
Typically 1000 (1ms or 48 samples per packet at 48kHz) for AES67 flows.

inputFields.name: deviceId

inputFields.description:
Allows setting a subscription to a device name when that device does not currently exist, typically because it is offline.

Subscriptions to unknown devices may be helpful when restoring a preset.

Dante resolves subscriptions by name, so this is a valid configuration. However, the subscription will remain unresolved until the transmitter device is online.

If set, 'allowSubscriptionToNonExistentChannel' must also be set since the channel name cannot resolve when the device is offline
inputFields.name: allowSubscriptionToNonExistentDevice

inputFields.description:
Allows setting a subscription to a channel name even when the transmitter device does not have a channel by that name

Subscriptions to unknown devices or channels may be helpful when restoring a preset.

Dante resolves subscriptions by name, so this is a valid configuration. However, the subscription will remain unresolved until the transmitter device has a channel by this name.

If this value is set to true, then additional checks (such as checking the media types of each channel match) will not be performed.
inputFields.name: allowSubscriptionToNonExistentChannel

inputFields.description:
The channel number on the device which will receive the subscription

Examples:
  - 1
  - 19

Channel numbers start at 1

This index is unique on the given device and is not media specific.
The index to use should be determined by first querying the channels on the device, finding the channel you want to modify, and then use that index.
inputFields.name: rxChannelIndex

inputFields.description:
The name of the device which is transmitting the media that you wish to subscribe to

    Device *names* are used in Dante subscriptions (rather than IDs) so that the the subscription will
    follow a device of that name, rather than a specific device of that ID.
    This allows the transmitting device to be swapped out for a device of the same name.

    Example: "AVIOAO2-51f9e7"

    To subscribe to an AES67 flow from an external SDP descriptor:
      - subscribedDevice must be set to the origin field in the external SDP descriptor. It must have the following format:
          <username> <sess-id> <sess-version> <nettype> <addrtype> <unicast-address>
    Example of a subscribedDevice value when subscribing to an AES67 flow: "- 987655 987657 IN IP4 10.0.1.4"
    allowSubscriptionToNonExistentChannel and allowSubscriptionToNonExistentDevice will be ignored for AES67 subscription, 


💡 An empty subscribedDevice and subscribedChannel will unsubscribe the channel
inputFields.name: subscribedDevice

inputFields.description:
The channel name on the device which is transmitting the media

Channel *labels* are used in Dante (rather than IDs) so that the the subscription will
follow the channel of that label, rather than a specific channel of that ID.
This allows the transmitting device rearrange it's transmit channels,
without needing to update the subscriptions on receiving devices.

Examples:
  "Audio L"
  "CH1"
  "01"

💡 An empty subscribedDevice and subscribedChannel will unsubscribe the channel
For AES67/RTP flow subscriptions, will be the channel/slot number of the channel: 
Example: for a flow with "a=rtpmap:96 L24/48000/2", the subscribeable channel are 1 and 2. (the 2 at the end of rtpmap indicates 2 channels)

types.name: __Schema

types.description:
The fundamental unit of any GraphQL Schema is the type. There are many kinds of types in GraphQL as represented by the `__TypeKind` enum.

Depending on the kind of a type, certain fields describe information about that type. Scalar types provide no information beyond a name, description and optional `specifiedByURL`, while Enum types provide their values. Object and Interface types provide the fields they describe. Abstract types, Union and Interface, provide the Object types possible at runtime. List and NonNull types compose other types.
